payload.claim: saffron/cell/session.py matches .saffron/policy.yaml's elevate_on: saffron/cell/**, so effective_risk will put this task at elevated regardless of the spec declaring no risk: field (it defaults to standard in frontmatter). At elevated, DESIGN.md's gate table makes size blocking rather than advisory, and the task sorts into DESIGN.md's level-4 ranking. This is correct, automatic repo behavior, not a bug, and the spec's measured token counts stay far under the ceiling either way, so nothing actually blocks. Separately, DESIGN.md's own risk table (the "Saffron breaks Saffron" row) says a self-task editing saffron/ should declare risk: elevated explicitly and put saffron/ in forbidden, which this spec does not do (it relies on the automatic elevate_on match and forbids only specific saffron/ subpaths). Since essentially every spec in this backlog touches saffron/ the same way, this DESIGN.md row reads as an illustrative risk/mitigation entry rather than an enforced per-spec rule, and no gate was found that requires a blanket saffron/ forbid.
